evidence.claim: Chase Center has a full basketball seating capacity of 18,064.
The Golden State Warriors have averaged 18,064 fans across home games at Chase Center in the 2026–27 NBA season, filling 100.0% of arena capacity.

plan.audience: Mostly local Bay Area adults aged about 25 to 55, including many season-ticket holders, tech and corporate groups, some families, and a few out-of-town visitors. Most drive, use rideshare, or take Muni. BART riders must transfer to Muni Metro (the T Third at Union Square/Market St beside Powell, or Muni from Embarcadero) or walk a long way.
plan.attendance_reason: This is a late-November NBA regular-season game, the Warriors hosting the Clippers on a Sunday evening. Warriors home games routinely sell out Chase Center's 18,064 basketball capacity, and both sourced claims point to a sellout. Keeping the announced or sold figure stays consistent with how the reference shares were measured, even though some ticket holders will not show up.
plan.reference_reason: Oracle Park to Embarcadero is the only measured San Francisco venue. Like Chase Center, it is not on BART, has limited parking and has strong competing Muni service. Chase Center is harder to reach from Embarcadero, though. It needs a Muni transfer or a roughly 2-mile walk, and the main Muni Metro link (the T via the Central Subway) connects near Powell rather than Embarcadero. So EMBR is used with a multiplier below 1.
multiplier_reasons: Parking: Chase Center has limited on-site parking, but Mission Bay garages and dedicated rideshare zones absorb a large share of fans, similar to or slightly more than at Oracle Park.

Walk: Oracle Park is a 15-minute walk from Embarcadero. Chase Center is not practical to walk to from Embarcadero and needs a Muni transfer, which adds wait time and pushes BART riders toward other stations or modes.
Crowd type: The NBA crowd is more affluent and corporate, with high season-ticket and premium-seat use. These fans favour driving and rideshare more than the Giants baseball crowd does.

Competing transit: The T Third, buses, Caltrain at 4th and King, and rideshare all serve Mission Bay directly. Among BART riders, many go through Powell (the T connection) or 16th St Mission instead of Embarcadero, splitting the volume this station would otherwise see.
Time of day: A Sunday 17:30 start is off-peak, with lower BART and Muni frequencies and longer transfer waits. The arrival window falls in daylight and dusk, so the effect is mildly negative.
plan.arrival_reason: The profile follows the EMBR night-game shape, nudged slightly earlier because BART riders need about 20 to 30 minutes to transfer and ride Muni to the arena. Doors open about 90 minutes before tip-off and there is no tailgating, so arrivals peak from 16:00 to 17:00. A sizable share comes through from 17:00 to 18:00 because NBA crowds arrive late, and a small tail of latecomers arrives after 18:00.
plan.end_reason: A regular-season NBA game typically runs about 2 hours 15 minutes to 2 hours 30 minutes. A 17:30 tip-off therefore ends around 19:45 to 20:00, assuming no overtime.
plan.departure_reason: This keeps the measured EMBR night shape, where the peak falls in the hour after the end hour. Some weight shifts into the end hour itself because the game ends near 20:00, and the Muni ride back puts most riders at Embarcadero between about 20:20 and 21:15. Early leavers make up the small share in the hour before the end. A tail runs past 22:00 for fans who stay for dinner or drinks or wait in Muni queues.
plan.weather_reason: The event is indoors and sold out. The day saw only 2.2 mm of light rain, with none in the hours around the event, so turnout is not affected.

other_stations.why: This is the main BART connection to the T Third via the Union Square/Market Street Muni Metro station, so many arriving and departing fans use it instead of Embarcadero.
It is the closest BART station by distance. Some fans walk the roughly 25 to 30 minutes or take a bus east to Mission Bay.
Some riders transfer to Muni Metro or walk from the Financial District instead of using Embarcadero or Powell.
